topic.name: The Norm of a Vector in Inner Product Spaces

question.text: An inner product on $V = \mathbb{R}^3$ is defined as $\langle \mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y} \rangle = 2x_1 y_1 + x_2 y_2 + 2x_3 y_3.$ Calculate the norm of the vector $\mathbf v= \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}$ under this inner product.
question.explanation:
The norm of a vector $\mathbf v$ with respect to an inner product $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ is defined as

\[ \begin{align*} \|\mathbf{v}\| = \sqrt{\langle \mathbf{v}, \mathbf{v} \rangle}. \end{align*} \]

Computing $\|\mathbf{v}\|$ using our definition, we get

\begin{align*} \|\mathbf{v}\| &= \sqrt{\langle \mathbf{v}, \mathbf{v} \rangle} \\[5pt] &=\sqrt{2\cdot (2\cdot 2) + 3\cdot 3 + 2 \cdot (4 \cdot 4)} \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{8 + 9 + 32} \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{49} \\[5pt] &= 7. \end{align*}

example.title: Calculating the Norm of a Vector With Respect to a Given Inner Product

question.text: Let $V=\mathbb{R}_2[t]$ be the vector space of all polynomials of degree at most $2,$ equipped with the inner product \[ \langle {x}(t), {y}(t) \rangle = x(0)y(0) + x(1)y(1) + x(2)y(2). \] Calculate the norm of the vector ${p}(t) = 2+t-t^2.$
question.explanation:
The norm of a vector $p(t)$ with respect to an inner product $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ is defined as

\[ \begin{align*} \| p(t) \| = \sqrt{\langle p(t), p(t) \rangle}. \end{align*} \]

Since ${p}(t) = 2+t-t^2,$ we obtain

\[ p(0)=2,\qquad p(1)= 2,\qquad p(2)=0. \]

Computing $\|p(t)\|$ using our definition, we get

\begin{align*} \|{p(t)}\| &= \sqrt{\langle p(t), p(t) \rangle} \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{p(0)p(0) + p(1)p(1) + p(2)p(2)} \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{[p(0)]^2 + [p(1)]^2 + [p(2)]^2} \\[5pt] &=\sqrt{(2)^2+ (2)^2 + (0)^2} \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{4 + 4 + 0} \\[5pt] &= \sqrt{8}\\[5pt] &= 2\sqrt 2. \end{align*}

example.title: Calculating the Norm of a Vector in an Inner Product Space of Polynomials

question.text:
Let $V=\mathcal{C}\left[0,4\right]$ be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $\left[0,4\right],$ equipped with the inner product

\[ \langle x(t),y(t) \rangle = \displaystyle\int_{0}^{4} x(t) y(t) \, \textrm{d}t. \]

Calculate the norm of the vector $f(t)= \sqrt t+1.$
question.explanation:
The norm of a vector $f(t)$ with respect to an inner product $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ is defined as

\[ \| f(t)\| = \sqrt{\langle f(t), f(t) \rangle}. \]

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

\begin{align*} \langle f(t),f(t) \rangle &= \displaystyle\int_{0}^{4} (f(t))^2 \, \textrm{d}t \\[5pt] &= \displaystyle\int_{0}^{4} (\sqrt t+1)^2 \, \textrm{d}t \\[5pt] &= \displaystyle\int_{0}^{4} (t+2\sqrt t+1) \, \textrm{d}t \\[5pt] &=\left.\left( \dfrac{t^2}{2}+\dfrac{4t\sqrt t}3+t \right)\right |_{0}^{4} \\[5pt] &= \left(8+\dfrac {32}3+4 \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{68}{3}. \end{align*}

Therefore,

\[ \| f(t)\| = \sqrt{\dfrac{68}{3}}. \]

example.title: Calculating the Norm of a Vector in an Inner Product Space of Continuous Functions

question.text: Let $V=\mathbb{R}_2[t]$ be the vector space of all polynomials of degree at most $2,$ equipped with the inner product \[ \eqalign{ \langle {x}(t), {y}(t) \rangle = x(1)y(1) + x(2)y(2) + x(3)y(3). }\] Normalize the vector $p(t) = t^2 - 3 t+4.$
question.explanation:
The norm of a vector $p(t)$ with respect to an inner product $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ is defined as \[ \| p(t)\| =\sqrt{\langle p(t), p(t) \rangle} . \]

Since $ p(t)= t^2- 3t+4,$ we obtain

\[ p(1) = 2, \qquad p(2) = 2, \qquad p(3) = 4 \]

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

\begin{align*} \langle p(t),p(t) \rangle &= [p(1)] ^2+ [p(2)]^2 + [p(3)]^2 \\[3pt] &= 2^2+2^2 + 4^2 \\[3pt] &= 4 + 4 + 16 \\ &=24. \end{align*}

Therefore,

\begin{align*} \|{p(t)}\| &= \sqrt{24} = 2\sqrt{6}. \end{align*}

To normalize the vector $p(t)$, we divide $p(t)$ by its norm $\|{p(t)}\| \mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} u(t)&=\dfrac{p(t)}{\|{p(t)}\|} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{t^2- 3t+4}{2\sqrt{6}} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\sqrt{6}}{12}(t^2-3t+4) \end{align*}

example.title: Normalizing a Vector in an Inner Product Space

question.text:
An inner product on $V = \mathbb{R}^3$ is defined as $\langle \mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y} \rangle = 3x_1 y_1 + x_2 y_2 + 3x_3 y_3.$

Normalize the vector $\mathbf v= \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}$ under this inner product.
question.explanation:
The norm of a vector $\mathbf v$ with respect to an inner product $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ is defined as

\[ \begin{align*} \|\mathbf{v}\| = \sqrt{\langle \mathbf{v}, \mathbf{v} \rangle}. \end{align*} \]

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

\begin{align*} {\langle \mathbf{v}, \mathbf{v} \rangle} &={3\cdot (2\cdot 2) + (-1)\cdot (-1) + 3 \cdot (1 \cdot 1)} \\[5pt] &= {12 + 1 + 3} \\[5pt] &= {16}. \end{align*}

Therefore,

\begin{align*} \|\mathbf v\| &= \sqrt{16} = 4. \end{align*}

To normalize the vector $\mathbf v$, we divide $\mathbf v$ by its norm $\|\mathbf v\| \mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} \mathbf u&=\dfrac{\mathbf v}{\|\mathbf v\|} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{4} \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}
